confirmed: The product is an offline single-page web experience named Afterthought.
The primary situation is a person leaving a high-pressure meeting and needing a three-minute reflection.
User data must remain on the local device; the product must not diagnose, treat, or decide for the user.
The final artifact must open by double-clicking a file.

assumptions.text: A dependency-free HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript is the safest meaning of offline and double-clickable.
The app may use localStorage for optional persistence, with an explicit clear action and no network requests.
Human response channel is unavailable, so copy, visual style, and interaction details are reversible agent decisions.

unresolved.question: Whether the user prefers a different visual tone or exact reflection prompts.

decisions.title: Local-only single file
decisions.decision: Deliver one self-contained afterthought.html with no external assets, fonts, libraries, or network calls.
decisions.rationale: This directly supports double-click launch and protects privacy under offline use.

decisions.title: Prompt, do not judge
decisions.decision: Use neutral questions and user-authored labels; avoid mental-health claims, scoring, diagnosis, or recommendations presented as truth.
decisions.rationale: The brief explicitly rejects a therapy product and substitution of the product's judgment for the user's.
